ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the right triangle $ABC$, with $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $AC=BC=2$, point $P$ is a moving point on segment $AB$. Connect $CP$, and rotate segment $CP$ $90^\circ$ clockwise around point $C$ to obtain segment $CQ$. Connect $PQ$ and $AQ$. What is the maximum area of $\triangle PAQ$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, rotate the line segment CP clockwise around point C to obtain line segment CQ, \\
$\therefore \angle PCQ=90^\circ$, CP=CQ,\\
$\therefore \angle ACP+\angle ACQ=90^\circ$,\\
Also, $\because \angle ACB=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle BCP+\angle ACP=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle BCP=\angle ACP$,\\
$\because AC=BC$,\\
$\therefore \triangle BPC\cong \triangle AQC$ (SAS),\\
$\therefore \angle B=\angle CAQ$, BP=AQ,\\
$\because BC=AC=2$,\\
$\therefore \angle B=\angle CAQ=\angle BAC=45^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle PAQ=\angle BAC+\angle CAQ=90^\circ$,\\
In $\text{Rt}\triangle ABC$, by the Pythagorean theorem AB= $\sqrt{BC^2+AC^2}=\sqrt{2^2+2^2}=2\sqrt{2}$,\\
Let BP=AQ=x, then $AP=2\sqrt{2}-x$,\\
$\therefore S_{\triangle PAQ}=\frac{1}{2}x(2\sqrt{2}-x)=-\frac{1}{2}(x^2-2\sqrt{2}x)=-\frac{1}{2}(x-\sqrt{2})^2+1$,\\
$\because a=-\frac{1}{2}<0$, the function opens downward, and the function has a maximum value,\\
When $x=\sqrt{2}$, $S_{\triangle PAQ_{\max}}=\boxed{1}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image: The diagram shows a right isosceles triangle ABC with A at the top, B at the lower left, and C at the lower right. AC is vertical, BC is horizontal, so \angle ACB=90^\circ and AC=BC=2. Point P lies on segment AB. Segment CP is drawn, then rotated 90^\circ clockwise about C to form CQ, with Q on the right side. Segments PQ and AQ are also drawn. Reasoning: Because CQ is obtained by rotating CP 90^\circ clockwise around C, we have CP=CQ and \angle PCQ=90^\circ. Let \alpha=\angle ACP. Since \angle ACB=90^\circ, the angle between BC and CP is \angle BCP=90^\circ-\alpha. After the quarter-turn, the angle between AC and CQ is also \angle ACQ=90^\circ-\alpha. Hence \angle BCP=\angle ACQ. Now BC=AC and CP=CQ, so \triangle BCP \cong \triangle AQC by SAS. Therefore BP=AQ, and also \angle CAQ=\angle B=45^\circ because \triangle ABC is a right isosceles triangle with AC=BC. Since P lies on AB, ray AP is collinear with AB, so \angle PAQ=\angle BAC+\angle CAQ=45^\circ+45^\circ=90^\circ. Thus \triangle PAQ is right-angled at A, with legs AP and AQ. Let AQ=BP=x. Since AB=\sqrt{2^2+2^2}=2\sqrt{2}, we get AP=AB-BP=2\sqrt{2}-x. So the area is S_{\triangle PAQ}=\frac12\,AP\cdot AQ=\frac12 x(2\sqrt{2}-x). This quadratic is maximized when x=\sqrt{2}, giving S_{\max}=\frac12\cdot\sqrt{2}\cdot\sqrt{2}=1. Therefore the maximum area of \triangle PAQ is 1.

S_{\triangle PAQ}=\frac12\,AP\cdot AQ=\frac12 x(2\sqrt{2}-x).
This quadratic is maximized when x=\sqrt{2}, giving S_{\max}=\frac12\cdot\sqrt{2}\cdot\sqrt{2}=1.
